items.q: A 58-year-old man with cirrhosis has a 3 cm hepatocellular carcinoma in segment 6 with no vascular invasion and no spread. He is unfit for surgery with severe COPD. The tumour board notes the lesion falls within Milan criteria and offers thermal destruction. Which modality best suits this small HCC within transplant criteria in an unfit patient?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Radiofrequency ablation.** Small hepatocellular carcinomas within Milan criteria suit radiofrequency ablation when surgery is refused or unfit.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: whole-liver radiation destroys functioning liver too.
- C: steroids never treat HCC.
- D: biopsy alone leaves the tumour untreated.
**Key point:** Small HCC within Milan means ablation.
items.kp: Small HCC within Milan criteria suits radiofrequency ablation.

items.q: A 63-year-old man undergoes radiofrequency ablation of a liver metastasis sitting against a large hepatic vein. Six months later imaging shows recurrence exactly at the vessel edge with a viable rim. The team discusses why the zone failed there. Which effect explains recurrence at the vessel edge after thermal ablation?
o: Heat-sink cooling from adjacent blood flow
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Heat-sink cooling from adjacent blood flow.** Vessels over 3 mm cool radiofrequency zones, inviting recurrence at the vessel edge.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: allergy causes hives, not rim recurrence.
- C: no stent is involved here.
- D: needle allergy is not a recognised entity.
**Key point:** Vessel edges recur through heat-sink.
r: Correct. Blood flow cools the zone.
items.kp: Heat-sink from vessels causes edge recurrence after ablation.

items.q: A 55-year-old woman has three small colorectal liver metastases and refuses hepatic resection. Her liver function is normal with no extrahepatic disease. The oncology team wants local destruction of each deposit. Which approach suits limited colorectal liver metastases when surgery is refused?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Percutaneous ablation of each deposit.** Colorectal metastases limited in number and size suit ablation when surgery is refused or unfit.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: antibiotics cannot kill metastases.
- C: transplantation is not indicated for colorectal spread.
- D: untreated deposits progress.
**Key point:** Limited colorectal mets suit ablation when surgery refused.
items.kp: Limited colorectal liver metastases suit ablation when surgery is refused.

items.q: A 67-year-old man with intermediate hepatocellular carcinoma and patent portal vein undergoes conventional TACE. Two days later he has fever to 38.4 degrees with right upper quadrant pain and nausea. Cultures are negative and he is stable. Which expected aftermath of TACE does this sterile fever with pain represent?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Post-embolisation syndrome.** Fever and pain after TACE with negative cultures and stability define post-embolisation syndrome needing supportive care.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: peritonitis gives guarding with positive signs.
- C: appendicitis localises to the right iliac fossa.
- D: infarction gives chest signs with ECG changes.
**Key point:** Fever after TACE is usually the syndrome.
r: Correct. Sterile fever means the syndrome.
items.kp: Fever and pain after TACE usually means post-embolisation syndrome.

items.q: A 60-year-old man with unresectable liver tumour and good reserve is planned for Y-90 radioembolisation. The mapping study injects macroaggregated albumin and scans the lungs and gut. The team must exclude excessive shunting before ordering the dose. Which mapping step must precede every Y-90 treatment?
o: Albumin scan for lung shunt and gut reflux
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Albumin scan for lung shunt and gut reflux.** A macroaggregated albumin scan maps lung shunting and gastrointestinal reflux before dosing, with excess shunt cancelling treatment.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: marrow biopsy never maps shunts.
- C: colonoscopy misses lung shunting.
- D: skin testing is irrelevant to microspheres.
**Key point:** Y-90 always needs an albumin shunt map first.
r: Correct. Albumin maps shunt and reflux.
items.kp: Y-90 radioembolisation needs an albumin shunt map first.

items.q: A 52-year-old woman with a 4 cm renal tumour near the collecting system is unfit for partial nephrectomy. The team wants ablation that visualises the zone and protects the drainage system. Which modality suits renal tumours hugging the collecting system?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Cryoablation with visible ice balls.** Cryoablation freezes with visible ice balls and suits renal tumours near the collecting system.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: whole-kidney radiation destroys function.
- C: embolising both kidneys causes failure.
- D: stents drain but never treat tumours.
**Key point:** Renal tumours near drainage suit freezing.
r: Correct. Ice balls protect collecting systems.
items.kp: Renal tumours near the collecting system suit cryoablation.

items.q: A 64-year-old man has a liver metastasis wrapped around the main bile duct. Thermal ablation would stricture the duct. The team wants cell kill without heat. Which non-thermal modality suits tumours hugging bile ducts or vessels?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Irreversible electroporation.** Electroporation uses electric pulses without heat, suiting tumours hugging bile ducts or vessels.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: maximum heat strictures the duct.
- C: blind lasers help nothing here.
- D: freezing whole livers is lethal.
**Key point:** Duct-hugging tumours mean electroporation.
items.kp: Tumours hugging ducts suit irreversible electroporation.

items.q: A 59-year-old man undergoes TACE for HCC with known portal vein thrombosis that was missed on planning. Within days he develops rapid liver failure with soaring bilirubin and encephalopathy. The team recognises combined loss of arterial and portal supply. Why must portal vein patency be confirmed before every TACE?
o: Dual supply loss causes liver failure
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Dual supply loss causes liver failure.** TACE removes arterial supply, so an already thrombosed portal vein leaves no perfusion and the liver fails.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: portal flow is the liver lifeline.
- C: arteries supply tumours and parenchyma.
- D: bilirubin rises in failure.
**Key point:** Confirm portal patency before TACE.
items.kp: Portal vein patency must be confirmed before TACE.

items.q: A 66-year-old woman receives Y-90 to the right lobe. Two weeks later she develops severe epigastric pain with endoscopy showing antral ulceration. Review of the mapping angiogram shows unrecognised reflux into the gastroduodenal artery. Which non-target injury of radioembolisation does this ulcer represent?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Gastric ulceration from refluxed spheres.** Refluxed Y-90 spheres ulcerate stomach and duodenum, the dreaded non-target injury.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: shrinkage never ulcerates stomach.
- C: allergy causes hives, not ulcers.
- D: gallstones were never implicated.
**Key point:** Post Y-90 ulcers mean refluxed spheres.
items.kp: Gastric ulceration after Y-90 means refluxed spheres.

items.q: A 57-year-old man has a subcapsular liver metastasis chosen for ablation. During withdrawal the operator burns the needle tract. The team explains this step seals the path. Why is tract ablation on withdrawal essential for subcapsular tumours?
o: It prevents seeding and bleeding along the path
It speeds up the biopsy report
items.exp:
**Answer: A - It prevents seeding and bleeding along the path.** Subcapsular tumours risk seeding and bleeding, needing tract ablation on withdrawal.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: reports come from labs, not burning.
- C: burning heats rather than cools.
- D: anaesthesia is still required.
**Key point:** Burn the tract in subcapsular ablation.
items.kp: Subcapsular ablation needs tract ablation on withdrawal.
